## AC5 amended by task f020-0960-2c42-4d61 (2026-08-12)

The probe classifier (`classify_probe_response`) is DROPPED from AC5's clause (a) — the
"one shared implementation in `adapters/jira_family/`, imported by both backends" list.

Why: bug `3b5f-1b21-ee14-4bdf` removed every consumer of the INBOUND absence-probe chain
(the producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the
`(inbound, probe)` dispatch arm, and `reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe`), leaving
`SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `probe_remote` dormant with zero callers. Task f020 executed the
operator's DELETE ruling: the port, `inbound_probe.py`, `adapters/jira/probe.py` and
`adapters/jira_family/probe.py` are all removed. The classifier's only callers were the
`probe_remote` implementations, so it went with them.

Effect on the both-backends claim: it is a SCOPE REDUCTION, not a regression. Clause (a)
now covers the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, and the link-relation vocabulary —
each still exactly one implementation imported by both backends. No unit was forked per
adapter; one shared unit ceased to exist because the capability it served ceased to exist.

ADR 0055 (jira-family sub-seam) and ADR 0028 (bound-but-absent) are updated to match.
Absence-vs-deletion discrimination remains OUTBOUND-owned
(`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`), unchanged by this.
